projects.title: Tadabbur
projects.description:
Tadabbur, a space to sit with the Qur'an and bring what's on your heart to it.

The idea was simple. Build something that helps you feel closer to Allah, not something that just works. So the design started from a feeling, not a feature list.

A few of the choices that came from that:

→ The name. Tadabbur is the slow, personal reading of the Qur'an, sitting with a verse until it means something to you. I wanted the whole app to feel like that.

→ A calm theme. Warm paper tones, a soft green, room to breathe. Opening it should feel like exhaling.

→ The word of Allah always set apart, in its own typeface, never blurred into anything human.

→ No streaks, no "you're 50% behind." A faith app should never make you feel like you're failing at faith.

Most of the work happened before I wrote any code. Exploring existing apps, seeing where they fell into the same clichés, and reading about tadabbur itself. I wanted every choice to come from the idea, not from colours I happened to like.

Walkthrough, live app and code below. Built with React Native, Expo and Supabase.

Would love feedback from people who know this space better than I do.

publications.title: DocDjinn: Controllable Synthetic Document Generation with VLMs and Handwriting Diffusion
publications.description: Effective document intelligence models rely on large amounts of annotated training data. However, procuring sufficient and high-quality data poses significant challenges due to the labor-intensive and costly nature of data acquisition. Additionally, leveraging language models to annotate real documents raises concerns about data privacy. Synthetic document generation has emerged as a promising, privacy-preserving alternative. We propose DocDjinn, a novel framework for controllable synthetic document generation using Vision-Language Models (VLMs) that produces annotated documents from unlabeled seed samples. Our approach generates visually plausible and semantically consistent synthetic documents that follow the distribution of an existing source dataset through clustering-based seed selection with parametrized sampling. By enriching documents with realistic diffusion-based handwriting and contextual visual elements via semantic-visual decoupling, we generate diverse, high-quality annotated synthetic documents. We evaluate across eleven benchmarks spanning key information extraction, question answering, document classification, and document layout analysis. To our knowledge, this is the first work demonstrating that VLMs can generate faithful annotated document datasets at scale from unlabeled seeds that can effectively enrich or approximate real, manually annotated data for diverse document understanding tasks. We show that with only 100 real training samples, our framework achieves on average  87% of the performance of the full real-world dataset. We publicly release our code and 140k+ synthetic document samples.

publications.title: DiffusionRec: Recognition-Guided Diffusion for Content-Aware Urdu Handwriting Generation
publications.publishedAt: International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition, ICDAR 2026 · Aug 23, 2026
publications.description: Robust Urdu handwriting recognition remains challenging due to the scarcity of content-aligned, word-level annotated data for cursive scripts. Reliable content-controlled generators can enable effective data augmentation and improve recognition accuracy. Previous research on Urdu handwriting generation has primarily focused on character and ligature-level generation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) have recently set a new baseline, with remarkable results in Text-to-Image generation. In this work, we propose DiffusionRec, a latent diffusion-based method that explicitly enforces recognition-guided content generation at the word level using a frozen pre-trained Conv-Transformer recognizer. Our model is trained on a dataset of 71,207 handwritten words. Generated images are evaluated using Frechet Inception Distance (FID) and Recognition Accuracy (Rec. Acc.) with independent external OCR system. Being first diffusion based approach for Urdu handwritten word generation, DiffusionRec achieves recognition accuracy of 45.2% demonstrating that recognition-guided diffusion can effectively produce content-aware handwritten words for low resource cursive scripts. Comparisons against state-of-the-art (SoTA) diffusion-based baselines highlight the potential of our framework for OCR data augmentation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first content-controlled diffusion-based system for Urdu word-level handwriting generation, establishing a foundation for low-resource cursive script recognition.

publications.title: Federated Unlearning with Clustered Asynchronous Aggregation and Ensemble Learning for Efficient Privacy-Preserving Document Analysis
publications.publishedAt: International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition 2025 · Sep 15, 2025
publications.description: Federated Learning (FL) enables decentralized model training while preserving privacy, but compliance with data erasure regulations poses significant challenges. Existing federated unlearning methods suffer from high computational costs or incomplete data removal. This paper introduces a novel federated unlearning framework that integrates Asynchronous Clustered Aggregation and Federated Ensemble Learning, ensuring efficient unlearning while maintaining model accuracy. By retraining only affected clusters instead of the entire model, our approach reduces retraining overhead by 2x while preserving 96–99% accuracy. Additionally, targeted noise injection prevents residual data influence, enhancing privacy protection. Evaluations on ICDAR-POD2017 and Invoices datasets demonstrate superior performance, achieving a 4–5% accuracy improvement over standard clustered aggregation. Our findings bridge the gap between privacy compliance and high-performance document analysis, offering a scalable and effective solution for federated unlearning.
